extractedText: I'Park Mall Turns to Fishing for Its Next Pop-Up HitFishing Pop-Up Runs Through the 16th Ballet, Car Detailing and Squishy Toys Come First Retailer Targets Narrow, Deep Consumer Tastes "We Will Keep Bringing New Taste-Driven Content"Finance|Published 2026.09.13. 09:10:05|By Lee Yong-sungutility@sedaily.com|Summary|SaveAAAVisitors browse the experiential pop-up store "Mallang Festa in Seoul," held last month at I'Park Mall's Yongsan branch. Photo courtesy of I'Park MallI'Park Mall, which has established itself as a hub for pop-up stores, has picked fishing as its next theme. The Yongsan complex has drawn crowds by turning narrow hobbies such as ballet, car detailing and paper folding into retail content, and is now extending that approach to fishing.Yongsan I'Park Mall is running "Big Catch POP-UP," a fishing- and sea-themed event, through the 16th on the third floor of Living Park at Dopamine Station The Pop-Up, according to retail industry sources on the 12th. Six brands are taking part, offering fishing gear as well as lifestyle goods inspired by local products from Tongyeong and by seafood. Rather than simply selling tackle, the pop-up bundles a range of tastes surrounding fishing and the sea into a single piece of content.In the fishing zone, Park Gwajang TV, a fishing YouTuber with 180,000 subscribers, displays gear and explains how to use it. The Tongyeong goods zone sells local items including clothing, key rings and beach towels inspired by oysters and seafood.I'Park Mall has spent this year turning specialized tastes into content as a strategy to draw shoppers offline. Instead of relying on big characters or well-known brands, it builds pop-ups around the hobbies that consumers pursue in depth.The mall has rolled out a series of pop-ups this year based on hobbies including ballet, car detailing, paper folding and squishy toys. In April, it opened a car-detailing pop-up called Detailing Studio, working with a popular car-wash YouTuber on content aimed at everyone from beginners to detailing enthusiasts.In June, it opened Ballet Atelier, targeting women in their 20s and 30s interested in recreational ballet and "balletcore" fashion, bringing together six brands specializing in ballet wear. Last month, it held Squishy Festa in Seoul, an experience-based pop-up featuring 11 popular domestic and overseas brands of squishy and stress-relief toys.These taste-driven pop-ups have translated into visitor traffic and sales. Ballet Atelier averaged more than 40 million won ($29,000) in daily sales. Squishy Festa in Seoul drew about 60,000 advance reservations alone as consumers flocked to try touch-focused products, and average weekday waiting times reached four to five hours. The car-wash and car-care pop-up also averaged more than 40 million won in daily sales.The strategy has also fueled growth at Dopamine Station, the mall's signature space. Since its official opening in August last year, Dopamine Station has surpassed 10 million cumulative visitors in one year, drawing about 30,000 people a day. The traffic has lifted the mall's overall performance, with Yongsan I'Park Mall's sales for January through July this year up 38% from a year earlier."As customers' tastes become more specialized, demand for varied experiences and content in shopping spaces is rising," an I'Park Mall official said. "In line with that change, I'Park Mall plans to continue introducing diverse and new taste-driven content and expand its points of contact with customers."#IParkMall#PopUpStore#Yongsan#DopamineStation#KoreanRetail#FishingPopUpOriginal reporting by Lee Yong-sung for Seoul Economic Daily.AI-translated from Korean.
